target.title: refactor(active-memory): split runtime modules
target.body:
Closes #106280

## What Problem This Solves

The Active Memory plugin runtime had grown to 4,182 lines in one entrypoint, combining configuration, session eligibility, prompt/query shaping, transcript evidence, recall execution, and plugin registration. That made reviews slower and made ownership boundaries harder to see.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps `index.ts` as the thin plugin registration surface and moves the existing runtime into focused sibling modules for types/constants, configuration, sessions, prompts/queries, transcript evidence, and recall execution. Runtime behavior, plugin exports, config/storage contracts, and the existing test helper surface remain unchanged.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Maintainers get smaller review surfaces and explicit one-way module dependencies for future Active Memory fixes.

## Evidence

- `corepack pnpm test extensions/active-memory` — 179 tests passed on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxdg70g4989v5nt5zzm4sdqs` ([Actions run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29242757122)).
- `corepack pnpm check:changed` — full extensions gate passed before the final main rebase on Testbox `tbx_01kxdfe5g1g3drfy63nxcmpe8x` (format, production/test typechecks, lint, guards, zero import cycles).
- Rebased-head changed gate passed focused tests and formatting, then stopped on Plugin SDK baseline drift reproduced with the same command on clean `origin/main`; no generated baseline files are changed here.
- Fresh autoreview of the exact rebased patch: no findings; patch correct with 0.99 confidence.

AI-assisted: yes. The implementation and generated diff were reviewed against the complete Active Memory test surface.
